This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
USE_SLANG - the default Yosys reader rejects `import` and silently breaks arrays of structs
The SRAM macro. The instance key is the flattened path, which is what the netlist calls it.
FS puts the macro's signal pins on its top edge, facing the free rows above it, and keeps its
Metal4 power columns vertical. x must stay 12 + 67.44 k so the columns stay under the stripes
(src/pdn_cfg.tcl). The lib keys name the process corner, because every corner here is nom_*.
The macro's two supplies both go to VPWR, the only supply a block has.
The default macro grid cannot power this macro. src/pdn_cfg.tcl runs the stripes through its
power columns, checks them, and stops the step if the grid has an open.
Magic's rules lack the SRAM exceptions of the KLayout deck, and the KLayout deck is the sign-off.
Magic reads the macro from its LEF, where the POWER stripes cross a Metal4 OBS at the
VDD!/VDDARRAY! split. tools/check_macro_power.py checks the real metal in the final GDS.
LVS treats the macro as a black box, because its insides are not LVS clean.
Stop a stuck route early and leave a report of what it is stuck on.
